# n8n Adapter Contract (source ↔ pipeline)

**Audience:** maintainers of the MCP **generator** (`Suite-GoCertius-MCP-Generator`) and the **pipeline** (`MCP_Market_Distribution`).

**Why this exists:** the n8n community node is generated by the pipeline from the MCP **source** (the `pending-to-publish/<mcp>/` repo, itself emitted by the generator). Every generator regen of the source can therefore silently break the published n8n node. This has happened repeatedly (EAD-ES v1.3.11 → v1.4.0), each time caught only by the n8n Creator Portal reviewer — slow and embarrassing.

**How this document cites code.** Anchors are `file#token`, never `file:line`. The token
is a literal string that must occur in the named file, and
`tests/unit/docs/n8n-adapter-contract-anchors.test.ts` fails the suite when one stops
resolving. Line numbers were the previous form and they rotted *inside a single epic*:
Story 18.6 verified its anchors against the tree, then 18.7 added one import to
`build-node-spec.ts` and one member to `types.ts` and every anchor below them was off by
one or two. A citation nobody can check is worth the same as no citation, and this
document is declared the live specification for the credential code — so the anchors are
now machine-checked.

This document is the contract that keeps regens safe. It is enforced automatically by the **`n8n_ux_compliance` gate** (Track B, Layer 1) which **fails the publish** before a non-compliant node ships. Treat a gate failure as "fix before publish", not "override".

---

## Division of ownership

| Concern | Lives in | Owner |
|---|---|---|
| n8n node code generation (templates, label casing, credential filtering) | `templates/n8n-adapter/*.hbs`, `src/adapters/n8n-adapter/*` | Pipeline (us) |
| Compliance gate | `src/gates/run-track-b-layer-1.ts` (`checkN8nUxCompliance`) | Pipeline (us) |
| Tool REST annotations (`// n8n-http:`) | `src/tools/*.ts` in the MCP source | **Generator** |
| `.distribution.yaml` (incl. `n8n_connector_display_name`) | MCP source root | **Generator** |
| `.env.example` (drives `server.json` env vars → credential screen) | MCP source root | **Generator** |
| Source README capability claims | MCP source `README.template.md` | **Generator** |

> The pipeline is built to be **resilient to source drift** wherever possible (brand casing, transport-var filtering, label casing are all rule-based, not per-MCP overrides). But some things the pipeline **cannot** infer, and one contract it must consume verbatim rather than infer at all, are the generator's to provide — see "Generator obligations".

---

## What the gate enforces (and the rule behind each)

Each rule maps 1:1 to a real n8n Cloud verification rejection. Source: <https://docs.n8n.io/integrations/creating-nodes/build/reference/ux-guidelines/>.

1. **No STUB operations in the UI.** Every operation shown must call a real REST endpoint. A `stub: true` entry in `OPERATION_META` means a source tool lost its parseable HTTP annotation → the operation throws "not available in n8n Cloud" at runtime. *Fix: restore the annotation in the source (generator) or remove the tool.*
2. **Brand display name casing.** The node `displayName` must read `EAD …` / `GoCertius …`, never the generic title-case fallback (`Ead`, `Gocertius`). Pipeline applies `BRAND_TOKEN_CASING` automatically; the generator should also set `n8n_connector_display_name` so the source is self-describing.
3. **Credential screen is an allowlist, never the MCP env set.** The n8n credential exposes **only** the fields the REST-direct `execute()` actually reads, keyed by `authStyle`. The `AuthStyle` union has four members (`build-node-spec.ts#AuthStyle`, `types.ts#authStyle`), but **only two are reachable by detection** (`build-node-spec.ts#detectAuthStyle`) — and those two are the only ones any emitted product can select. Reachable first:

   - **`user-key`** → `baseUrl` + `userKey`, and nothing else (user-facing products: GoCertius / EAD Enterprise Suite). The n8n user signs in as themselves with a single long-lived **User Key** (`MCP_AUTH_USER_KEY`, ~12 months, issued out-of-band) exchanged at `POST /user-keys/session` with the key in the **body** (`{"key": "…"}`) → `{"jwt": "…"}`. Because the JWT is short-lived and minted once per `execute()`, a `401` on any per-item call re-mints it once and replays the call. `baseUrl` is emitted by the template rather than derived from the allowlist, but its **requiredness** is read off the emitted `MCP_API_BASE_URL#isRequired` (`build-node-spec.ts#baseUrlRequired`) — required on these two products, optional on EAD Factory.
   - **`oauth2-client-credentials`** → `baseUrl` **only** (EAD Factory). Since Epic 16 the credential `extends = ['oAuth2Api']` (`credentials.ts.hbs#oAuth2Api`), so n8n's own base type supplies Client ID / Client Secret / Access Token URL / Scope and acquires, caches and refreshes the token itself. `buildCredentials` therefore returns `[]` for this style (`build-node-spec.ts#buildCredentials`) and the template emits `baseUrl` plus the hidden `grantType`/`authentication` pair and no env-derived props at all (`credentials.ts.hbs#grantType`). The `MCP_SVC_*` allowlist entry survives for the detection discriminator and for the gate's mirror, not because a prop is rendered from it. `MCP_SVC_INTROSPECT_URL` is **not** a credential — it configures the server's *inbound* bearer validation, not the node's *outbound* token fetch, so it stays out of the allowlist.
   - `email-password` (`baseUrl` + `email`/`password`) and `okta-client-credentials` (`baseUrl` + `oktaTokenUrl`/`oktaClientId`/`oktaClientSecret`/`oktaScope`) are **rendered but unreachable**. The template branches still exist (`credentials.ts.hbs#email-password`, `credentials.ts.hbs#oktaTokenUrl`) and tests still drive the `email-password` literal, so do **not** delete them — but no emitted `.env.example` declares `MCP_AUTH_EMAIL` or `OKTA_TOKEN_URL` any more, detection cannot select either (it throws instead of defaulting), and the gate would now reject the props the first one produces: Epic 18 dropped `email`/`password` from `ALLOWED_CREDENTIAL_PROPS` (`run-track-b-layer-1.ts#ALLOWED_CREDENTIAL_PROPS`). Read them as "still compiles", not as "still shipped". <!-- retired-auth-history -->

   > **`MCP_SVC_*` means two different things and the docs must not flatten it.** On EAD Factory it is the **outbound** service-account credential (`MCP_SVC_TOKEN_URL`/`_CLIENT_ID`/`_CLIENT_SECRET`/`_SCOPE`, declared in `EAD-Factory-MCP:.env.example`). On GoCertius / EAD Enterprise Suite the same-named `MCP_SVC_INTROSPECT_URL` / `MCP_SVC_CLIENT_ID` / `MCP_SVC_CLIENT_SECRET` configure the server's **inbound** Bearer introspection and authenticate nothing upstream (declared in `GoCertius_MCP:.env.example`). Same names, opposite direction.

   *History (Epic 14):* `sessionToken` — a node-only pasted-JWT field with no backing env var, added in Epic 14.1 / PR #231 — was removed, together with the `GET /session-info/{email}` **auth-time** type check that refused OpenID/SSO accounts. With `EXTRA_CREDENTIAL_FIELDS` losing its only entry, the node-only-field mechanism went too: every credential field is now derived from the env-var allowlist, which is why the emitted contract is the whole story. Note that `session_info` is **not** an n8n operation on either product: the tool file exists in both source trees, but its `// n8n-http: GET /profile` annotation sits on line 9, outside the 8-line header slice `readToolHttpInfo` reads (`build-node-spec.ts#readToolHttpInfo`), so the adapter omits it. "Present in the source" ≠ "an operation in the node".

   *History (2026-09-07, Epic 18):* this rule used to carry a standing "do not release the User Key flow until `GET /profile` lands" block. That gap was real — `session_info` was keyed on an email a User-Key credential never has, so `userId` was unobtainable — and it is closed: `GET /profile` ships as the `profile_get` tool (`GoCertius_MCP:src/tools/profile_get.ts`, annotation on the second line) and as a published n8n operation (`Gocertius.node.ts`, *Get Profile*). Generation then deleted email, password and the pre-seeded token from the server, so the User Key is not one option among several — it is the only flow, and it is mandatory.

   **Auth-style detection precedence matters** (`build-node-spec.ts#detectAuthStyle`). The live rule is three `if`s in this order: `MCP_AUTH_USER_KEY` ⇒ `user-key`, checked **before** `MCP_SVC_TOKEN_URL` ⇒ `oauth2-client-credentials`, itself before `OKTA_TOKEN_URL` ⇒ `okta-client-credentials`. The order is load-bearing for the same reason it always was, only with a different discriminator: GoCertius/EAD-ES declare an `MCP_SVC_*` pair of their own — for **inbound** introspection, not for signing in — so checking the service-account variable first misclassifies them as `oauth2` and produces a credential with an empty token URL ("Invalid URL" on every saved credential). Note the discriminator is `MCP_SVC_TOKEN_URL` specifically, never the `MCP_SVC_*` prefix, precisely because the prefix is ambiguous across products. Only a product with **no** user-key surface (EAD Factory) is a pure service account. **FR61: there is no default.** A descriptor matching none of the three discriminators throws (the final statement of `build-node-spec.ts#detectAuthStyle`) rather than falling back to a style whose allowlist intersects the declared variables to the empty set — a credential form with zero authentication fields is indistinguishable from success at every gate.

   This is an **allowlist** (`build-node-spec.ts#NODE_READABLE_CREDENTIAL_ENV_VARS`), not a denylist — so any MCP-server runtime var (`MCP_HTTP_*`, `MCP_ALLOW*`, `MCP_OPENID_*`, `PORT`, …) is dropped automatically without a pipeline change. The gate's `credential_allowlist` check backstops it: any credential prop outside `ALLOWED_CREDENTIAL_PROPS` fails the publish. *History: a denylist let `MCP_OPENID_*`/`PORT` leak (v1.2.19) and `MCP_HTTP_*`/`MCP_ALLOW*` leak again (v1.3.x) — the allowlist closes the class permanently. When the generator renamed EAD Factory's `OKTA_*` → `MCP_SVC_*` (v1.1.0), `detectAuthStyle` still keyed on `OKTA_TOKEN_URL` and silently fell back to email-password, producing a credential with only `baseUrl` — hence the `oauth2-client-credentials` style, and hence the throw that replaced the fallback.*

   **To add a genuinely new auth field, or a new auth style, extend all of these together** — this list is canonical; the shorter one in the code comment directly above `build-node-spec.ts#NODE_READABLE_CREDENTIAL_ENV_VARS` defers to it, and Epic 18 proved every member is mandatory (a rename that touched only some of them shipped a form with no authentication fields):

   1. the `AuthStyle` union in `build-node-spec.ts#AuthStyle` **and** the `authStyle` union in `types.ts#authStyle` — both declarations, they are separate;
   2. the detection branch itself (`build-node-spec.ts#detectAuthStyle`);
   3. `NODE_READABLE_CREDENTIAL_ENV_VARS` (the allowlist);
   4. `CREDENTIAL_PROP_NAME_MAP` (env var → credential prop name);
   5. `execute()` in `templates/n8n-adapter/node.ts.hbs`;
   6. the credential class and its test in `templates/n8n-adapter/credentials.ts.hbs`;
   7. the gate's `ALLOWED_CREDENTIAL_PROPS` in `src/gates/run-track-b-layer-1.ts`.

4. **No dead chat code / copy.** A node without `chat_*` operations must not ship chat handling or advertise "certified chats" in its README. Gated by `spec.hasChat`.
5. **Label casing.** Field labels use `IDs` (not `IDS`); operation labels are verb-first (`Create Case File`, not `Case File Create`). Both are produced automatically by the pipeline.

## Which scanner version the `official_linter` gate runs

**Always `latest`.** `package.json` declares `"@n8n/scan-community-package": "latest"` on purpose — the gate exists to predict the n8n Creator Portal's verdict, so it tracks whatever n8n publishes as stable rather than a version we pinned once and forgot. Do not pin it back to an exact version without a reason written here.

Consequences to keep in mind:

- **`latest` only moves when the lockfile does.** `--frozen-lockfile` installs whatever `pnpm-lock.yaml` resolved — `0.27.1` today — so the specifier alone does not keep the gate current. Refresh it deliberately (`pnpm update @n8n/scan-community-package`, commit the lockfile) when you want the gate to track a newer stable, and re-measure the gate against a known-bad tree afterwards. Observed 2026-09-02.
- **Do not read `beta` results as the portal's verdict.** As of 2026-07-22 the tags are `latest`/`stable` = `0.27.1` and `beta` = `0.29.1`. They behave very differently, and only the first is what n8n ships as stable.
- **A floating dependency means the module's shape can change under us.** `SOURCE_FILE_PATTERNS` only exists from 0.29.x; both consumers (`run-track-b-layer-1.ts` and `normalize-generated-node.ts`) must therefore treat it as optional and fall back to `SOURCE_FILE_PATTERNS_FALLBACK`. Spreading the missing export threw `sourceFilePatterns is not iterable` and took the gate down. Same care applies to any other export or signature: `analyzePackage` gained a second parameter in 0.29.x, which is safe only because it is defaulted.
- **Scanning a published tarball is NOT equivalent to scanning a source tree.** Up to 0.28.x the scanner globs `.ts`/`.d.ts`, and our tarballs ship only compiled `.js` (`files: ["dist"]`) — so `npx @n8n/scan-community-package <our-package>` matches nothing, every AST rule no-ops, and it reports a **false green** (it passed `ead-factory@1.2.1`, which had 96 real violations). The gate is unaffected because it scans the *generated source dir*, where the `.ts` globs match: verified on that same 1.2.1 tree, 0.27.1 reports 98 violations. When you want to check a *published* package, use 0.29.x, which resolves the npm provenance back to the GitHub source and lints that.

## Generator obligations

When adding or regenerating a tool in the generator, ensure:

1. **Custom/handwritten tool files carry an HTTP annotation** the pipeline can parse, as the **first 8 lines** of the file. Two accepted forms:
   - `// Sourced from operation: <OpName> (POST /path/{param})` — note the **`(METHOD /path)`** suffix is mandatory.
   - `// n8n-http: POST /path/{param}` — preferred for custom overrides.
   A tool with neither has no REST endpoint and is **omitted from the n8n node** (the REST-direct adapter cannot execute it), with a diagnostic note in the build output. This is correct for intentionally custom-only tools (e.g. `evidence_upload`, which does local hashing + multi-step S3 orchestration with no single backing endpoint). But it means a *real* endpoint whose annotation is accidentally dropped will silently disappear from the node — so always check the "OMITTED from the n8n node" notes after a regen. (This is exactly how `notification_certificate_get.ts` broke in v1.4.0: it had `// Sourced from operation: CreateNotificationCertificateController_run` **without** the `(METHOD /path)` suffix, so it shipped as a throwing stub; the adapter now omits such tools instead.)
2. **`.distribution.yaml` sets `n8n_connector_display_name`** to the brand-correct string (`"EAD Enterprise Suite"`, `"GoCertius"`). The pipeline has a brand-casing fallback, but the source should be self-describing.
3. **`.distribution.yaml` emits `manager_api_base_paths` for a MULTI-MANAGER product, and `query_param_style` where the API needs it.** These are the two things the pipeline genuinely cannot infer, and they are the **gates** for Stories 13.3/13.4/13.6 — absent, those stories are silently inert (the node still builds, it just keeps the old, wrong behavior):

   | Field | Gates | Effect when absent |
   |---|---|---|
   | `manager_api_base_paths` (`{evidence: /digital-trust, signature: /signature-manager, …}`) | 13.3 per-manager base path, 13.4 manager-aware naming | one credential can't serve every manager; resources render `Evidence`/`Notification`/`Signature` instead of `… Manager`, operations `Search Evidence Case File` instead of `EM Search Case File` |
   | `query_param_style: flat` | 13.6 query serialization | the node emits `?filter[size]=2`, which EAD Factory's API **ignores** — a search returns unfiltered results (observed: 50 records instead of 2) |

   `manager_api_base_paths` is a plain string→string map; `query_param_style` is `'bracket'` (default, omit it) or `'flat'`. Only a product whose managers sit behind different gateway prefixes needs the first; single-API products (gocertius, ead-enterprise-suite) correctly omit both and are unaffected.

   **Status 2026-09-02: both fields are now emitted for EAD Factory — 13.3/13.4/13.6 are NO LONGER inert.** Verified against `EAD-Factory-MCP@main`'s `.distribution.yaml`: `manager_api_base_paths` carries four managers (`evidence: /digital-trust`, `signature: /signature-manager`, `notification: /notifications`, **`chat: /chat-bot-manager`** — one more than the Epic 13 design listed) and `query_param_style: flat` is set. `Suite-GoCertius-MCP-Generator#66` delivered.

   **Read this before the next EAD Factory release.** All three behaviours flip on the next regeneration, with no pipeline change to announce them:

   - the credential's base URL becomes the **gateway root** (13.3) → an existing EF credential pointed at a manager-specific URL now builds wrong URLs;
   - resources are renamed `… Manager` and operations gain `EM`/`SM`/`NM` prefixes (13.4) → saved workflows that pin `resource`/`operation` break;
   - query serialization becomes flat (13.6) → this one is a **fix**; filters start working.

   So EF's next publish is breaking for saved credentials *and* saved workflows, stacked on top of Epic 16's credential rename. It needs the Epic 14/16 treatment — explicit release notes and a user warning — not a routine regen. Registered in `_bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/contract-register-2026-09-02.md`.

   *Historical note: from 2026-07-15 to 2026-09-02 this section said the fields were absent and the stories inert. They stopped being inert without anyone noticing, which is the same blind spot that let `logo_svg_dark_path` block every release for six weeks (#243). The weekly `regression-e2e` schedule (#245) is what now reads these files on a cadence; it still cannot tell us that a **behavioural** field appeared, only that the schema still parses.*

4. **`.env.example` is the credential contract — and since Epic 18 it carries a real n8n obligation.** Two halves, and only the first is unchanged:

   - *Still true:* `.env.example` may contain any MCP-server runtime config — transport, CORS, OpenID, `PORT` — because the Docker/self-hosted MCP server reads it; **keep it there**. The n8n adapter derives its credential surface from an allowlist (rule 3), so it is immune to whatever else the generator adds, with no pipeline change needed.
   - *No longer true:* that this makes `.env.example` "a pipeline-owned boundary with no n8n obligation". Per **FR61** the credential form is derived from, and only from, the emitted contract: each variable's `# isSecret:` decides whether the field is masked, its `# isRequired:` decides whether the field is required (never inferred from secrecy — `MCP_API_BASE_URL` is required and non-secret), its `# description:` becomes the field's description, and **detection itself** keys on a declared variable name. Deleting or renaming `MCP_AUTH_USER_KEY` does not degrade the form, it **fails the build** (`build-node-spec.ts#detectAuthStyle` throws). Renaming any of the three auth-style discriminators, or flipping an `isRequired`, is a breaking change to every saved n8n credential and must be released as one.

## When the gate fails

The error report tells you which rule and how to fix. Route per the table above: if it's a label/casing/credential-filter issue, fix in the pipeline; if it's a missing annotation, missing `n8n_connector_display_name`, or a README capability claim, file an issue against `Suite-GoCertius-MCP-Generator`.

Never publish by bypassing the gate. A red gate is the system doing its job.

## Verify CI yourself — a check nobody reads is worth nothing

Opening a PR, merging it, or dispatching a pipeline is not the end of the task. **You must verify the result of every process you set in motion** — wait for the run and read its real status (`gh pr checks <n>`, `gh run view <id> --log-failed`), then report what actually happened, not what you expected to happen. Two rules follow from this:

1. **Never claim a check "will run" or "passed" without looking.** Know exactly what each workflow validates before you cite it. In particular, `regression-e2e.yml` invokes `publish.yml@main` cross-repo, so it exercises the pipeline code on `main` — **not** the TypeScript in your PR. And there is currently **no `pull_request` workflow that runs the unit-test suite or the ESLint/`official_linter` pass**, so for a pipeline-code PR the automated evidence is *local only* unless you add one. Do not present a green `regression-e2e` as proof your PR's code is sound.
2. **If a check runs in this repo, it is ours to fix.** "Pre-existing" or "belongs to another repo" is a diagnosis to prove, not an excuse to move on. A CI job that is chronically red trains reviewers to ignore the red X — which defeats the entire point of having it.

3. **`regression-e2e` only exercises its deep gates AFTER a merge — so review that post-merge run.** On a PR it (a) tests `publish.yml@main`, not the PR's code, and (b) resolves each source to its already-published `@main` version, so the ledger marks every target idempotent and skips Track A L2/L3, Track B, Track C and all publishers — only coherence + Track A L1 + ledger + audit actually run. Its real value lands after the change is on `main` and the next run (or a manual `workflow_dispatch`) hits a not-yet-published version. **Therefore: after merging any pipeline change to `main`, you must open the resulting `regression-e2e` run and confirm it is green — that is the first time the deep gates see the merged code.** Accepting "green on the PR" as sufficient is exactly the trap this rule closes.

*Example (2026-07-16): `regression-e2e` had been red on `main` since May because its source-version pins had gone stale — the dry-run clones each source @ main, but the "expected version" came from a hardcoded pin, so the coherence gate flagged a mismatch on every PR. Fixed by resolving each source's version from its repo @ main at run time (`resolve-versions` job) instead of pinning; the gate keeps its real value (catching an internally-incoherent snapshot) without the false positive.*
